Vibha Padalkar: 
Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining our earnings conference call for the half 
year ended September 30, 2026. Our results along with the investor presentation, press release, 
and regulatory disclosures are available on our website and with the stock exchanges.  
 
Joining me on today’s call are Niraj Shah, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer; 
Vineet Arora, Executive Director and Chief Business Officer; Eshwari Murugan, Appointed 
Actuary and Chief Actuary; and Kunal Jain, Head - Investor Relations, Business Planning and 
Strategy. 
 
Let me begin with the broader environment. In its latest policy, the Reserve Bank of India 
raised its FY2027 growth projection to 7.1% from 6.7%, reflecting continued resilience in 
domestic economic activity, while the fiscal position remains well managed. 
 
At the same time, the RBI raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and moved to 
a stance of calibrated tightening, given elevated energy prices and a below-normal monsoon, 
which remain the key risks to inflation. Broadly, we expect macro conditions to remain stable, 
which in turn should support steady growth for the life insurance industry. 
 
Moving on to business performance. In Q2, individual weighted received premium grew 11%, 
ahead of the private industry at 10%, with market share improving 10bps to 16.2% in Q2. This 
took our H1 individual APE growth to 9%. Overall APE grew faster, at 13% in Q2 and 11% in 
H1. The number of individual policies grew 9% in H1, ahead of the industry. We expect to 
sustain this momentum and grow in line with the industry in FY27.  
 
Growth was broad-based across channels. Individual APE sourced by HDFC Bank grew 12% 
in Q2, slightly ahead of company growth. We have sustained our counter share, building on 
the momentum we saw late in Q1 and supported by deeper engagement with the bank across 
branches, products and processes, and we expect our share to steadily improve going forward. 
 
Other bancassurance partnerships also grew well, delivering a YoY growth of 13% in Q2. We 
are pleased to announce our new bancassurance partnership with J&K Bank and we look 
forward to scaling the relationship, deepening our presence across its network and extending 
our reach to a wider customer base. Other non-bank corporate alliances clocked robust growth 
in Q2 of 13%.  
 
Agency continues to grow faster than the company and the broader agency market, at 13% in 
H1, and our position in this channel has strengthened. Investment in expanding our branch 
network is yielding good results: branches opened over the last 30 odd months now contribute 
about 17% of agency business, versus 12% a year ago. 
 
Agent additions and activation remain healthy, and frontline productivity has improved. The 
channel’s mix is also strengthening, with protection and annuity together contributing about

30% versus 15% in the previous period. Even as we continue to perform well across our 
partner channels, investing in and building our proprietary channels remains a key priority.  
 
Next, on product mix. In H1, unit-linked products contributed 45% of individual APE, non-par 
savings 22%, annuity 12%, participating products 13% and retail protection 8%. Retail 
protection grew 33% in H1, a two-year CAGR of 30%, with growth broad-based across 
geographies and customer cohorts. Its share of individual APE rose to 8% from about 7% last 
year. 
 
Rider attachment also continues to be healthy, and protection and riders together now account 
for 11% of individual APE. In the second half of last year, protection grew 57% following the 
GST exemption. This year, we expect growth to normalize as the base starts to kick in and 
remain strong on a 2-year CAGR basis. Our retail sum assured grew by 21% in H1, with 
Market Share increasing by 20bps to 15.4% in H1. 
 
Credit protect grew 19% in H1, with growth broad-based across portfolios. Non-par savings 
and annuity together contributed 34% of individual APE. With interest rates at elevated levels, 
this is an opportune time for customers to lock in long-term guaranteed returns. 
 
In line with our focus on driving growth this year, we will continue to use the current interest 
rate environment to sharpen the value we offer customers across both segments. Unit-linked 
demand remained resilient despite equity market volatility.  
 
Moving on to financial and operating metrics. Value of new business for H1 was ₹2,037 crore, 
a growth of 12%, ahead of APE growth. VNB growth for Q2 was 15%. New business margin 
was 24.7%, compared with 24.5% in H1 FY2026. 
 
The improvement was driven by a strong product mix and the continued mitigation of the GST 
impact we had absorbed last year. Embedded Value stood at ₹66,461 crore, with rolling 12-
month operating ROEV of 14.9%. 
 
Profit after tax for H1 was ₹1,119 crore, a growth of 13%. Assets under management stood at 
₹4.1 trillion, up 14% year-on-year. Our 13th month persistency stood at 83% and 61st month 
at 66%. Persistency was softer on renewal collections in our unit-linked book amidst market 
volatility, and in a specific cohort of non-par business written last year. 
 
We are working closely with our distribution partners and expect some recovery by the end of 
the year. Our solvency ratio stood at 180% as of September 30, 2026, well above the 
regulatory requirement of 150%. The Board has approved raising up to ₹500 crore through 
subordinated debt, which we expect to complete during the current quarter, further 
strengthening our capital position as we invest for growth.  
 
Moving on to subsidiaries and ESG. The Pension business continued to scale, with assets 
under management of ₹1.8 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, up 28% year-on-year. We also

continue to see an attractive long-term opportunity in GIFT City for USD-denominated 
insurance solutions.  
 
On ESG, our MSCI ESG rating was upgraded to AAA from AA. This reflects our leadership 
in governance and the progress we have made across each element of our ESG framework.  
 
Finally, on the regulatory front. IRDAI has released consultation papers on the economics of 
insurance distribution, which propose significant changes for the industry. The regulator has 
encouraged industry participants to share their feedback supported by data and keeping 
policyholder interest at the centre of the conversations. 
 
As an industry, our shared goal is Insurance for All by 2047. Getting there will require 
widening reach, building greater transparency and trust, and improving affordability for 
customers. More attractive products and distribution partners who bring advice, service and 
reach to customers will remain central. 
 
Our business has been built around many of the principles the consultation emphasises: 
diversified distribution with a growing proprietary channel, a calibrated expense model and a 
long-standing focus on quality of business and customer outcomes. 
 
This positions us well to keep investing in deepening and widening our reach. With the 
consultation still under way and the industry engaging with the regulator, we will be better 
placed to comment on specifics once the framework is finalised. 
 
To conclude, momentum is building across our business. We grew ahead of the industry in 
quarter 2, growth was broad-based across channels, our investment in agency continues to 
deliver, and our VNB growth has been ahead of APE. We remain confident in the long-term 
opportunity for the industry and in our ability to further strengthen our position within it.  
 
For a more detailed discussion of our performance and outlook, please refer to the investor 
presentation. We will now be happy to take your questions.
